item.title: Supply Chain and AI Threat Intelligence Platform - v1.1.18 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Version 1.1.18 **NEW — BOD 26-04 Risk-Tier Classification** CISA revoked Binding Operational Directive 22-01 on June 10, 2026 and replaced it with BOD 26-04, Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk. Flat KEV deadlines are gone; remediation timelines are now driven by a four-variable risk model. \- New view: Federal ConMon > BOD 26-04 Risk-Tier Classification. Each KEV-matched vulnerability is classified per application against CISA's four variables — public exposure, KEV status, exploit automatability, and post-exploitation technical impact — and given a computed remediation deadline ranging from "fix on next system upgrade" to 3 days with mandatory forensic triage. \- The remediation-timeline matrix ships as a readable lookup (lookups/bod\_2604\_matrix.csv) so it can be opened and audited against CISA's own table rather than taken on trust. \- Deadlines are anchored at the earlier of the CVE's KEV catalog listing date and its first detection in your environment, matching CISA's stated timeline start. \- Applications with no exposure tag are treated as publicly exposed for deadline purposes — CISA's stated default when exposure is unknown — and are labeled provisional rather than silently treated as not exposed. They also appear in a dedicated assessment queue. \- KEV-listed vulnerabilities missing enrichment data have the missing dimension filled worst case and are labeled provisional. Enrichment is always published for KEV CVEs, so a gap is an ingestion issue, never grounds for a more relaxed deadline. \- Proxy disclosure is shown in-product: "Automatable" is derived from EPSS percentile and "Technical Impact" from the known-ransomware KEV field falling back to CVSS. These are proxies, not CISA's SSVC decision points, and are labeled as such on every row. \- New Setup section: Asset Exposure Tagging, for declaring which applications are publicly exposed. \- The classification search ships disabled and is enabled from Setup. NEW — Silent-Source Detection & Coverage-Evidence Manifest SCIP's AI-threat detection is a passive, out-of-band watcher over telemetry you route into Splunk — it only sees what reaches it. This release closes the blind spot where a telemetry source going silent looks identical to a source with nothing to report. \- New view: AI Telemetry Coverage. Enrolled telemetry sources are tracked with a last-seen high-water mark and a status of reporting, silent, or unknown — unknown is never presented as healthy; a source with no data yet stays visibly unassessed rather than assumed clean. \- Silent-source detection fires when a previously-reporting enrolled source goes quiet. \- Coverage-evidence manifest is an AU-12-aligned attestation artifact: proof that AI-monitoring coverage was complete and unbroken over the reporting period, for FedRAMP ConMon evidence packages. \- New Setup section: Section 7, AI Telemetry Source Coverage, for declaring which AI/LLM telemetry sources SCIP should expect to see. **CHANGED — BOD 22-01 relabeled historical** \- The BOD 22-01 SLA Compliance view is now "BOD 22-01 (Historical)" and displays a revocation notice in every license state. The claim that this view constitutes required federal authorization evidence has been removed. Due dates remain accurate as the dates CISA assigned while the directive was in effect. \- FedRAMP POA\&M workbook column headers are intentionally unchanged. "Binding Operational Directive 22-01 tracking" and "Binding Operational Directive 22-01 Due Date" are the official FedRAMP template's literal column titles, and 3PAOs and automated tooling expect that exact text. See docs/POAM\_FIELD\_MAPPING.md. \- POA\&M and BOD documentation updated to historical framing. **FIXED — Version-match consistency (SCIP-114)** \- SBOM components whose version string cannot be parsed were previously dropped from the NVD Version Range Correlation output while seven other paths treated them as fully confirmed. All eight consuming searches now apply the same filter and carry version\_match and match\_type through to their outputs, so every downstream consumer can distinguish a confirmed match from an unconfirmed one. \- Auto Remediation Creator now creates tickets only for confirmed matches. Unconfirmed findings that would otherwise qualify are routed to a review queue instead — inspect with | inputlookup scip\_version\_needs\_review.csv. No ticket is ever auto-generated from an unconfirmed match. \- PCI DSS 6.3.3 reports "Needs Review — Unconfirmed version matches" when the only open CVE evidence comes from unconfirmed matches, rather than a hard Gap or Pass. Confirmed vulnerabilities still drive Gap as before. **CHANGED — Navigation** \- The app menu is organized into three groups: Risk & Compliance, AI Threat Detection, and Federal ConMon, plus Home, Component Search, Setup, About, and Search. No view was added, removed, renamed, or tier-gated by this change. FIXED — Hardening and maintenance \- The AI application mapping and license blocklist commands now check license status in addition to tier in their dispatch guards. An expired paid account can no longer write to these commands' configuration via direct SPL. \- POA\&M audit-trail protection (AU-9): every audit write is also forwarded to a write-once index (poam\_audit) so an edited or deleted KV record leaves the original event intact and independently discoverable. The poam\_audit index must be provisioned; see indexes.conf.example. \- POA\&M audit read access (AU-9): the write-once protection above only closes half the gap if nobody can read the surviving copy. scip\_admin now has read access to the poam\_audit index; scip\_analyst and scip\_viewer do not, matching this app's least-privilege pattern for admin-only surfaces. \- Executive Summary now links directly to the Compound Risk view. \- Telemetry remains strictly opt-in with an unchanged payload; an unused development placeholder token was removed. No secret ships in the package. No licensing or crypto surface was modified in this release. bin/scip\_license\_core.py and bin/scip\_ed25519\_verify.py are byte-identical to the prior release.


Short Description:
Unifies software supply chain risk (SBOM/SCA), MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detection, and nine-framework compliance in one Splunk app — with FedRAMP-ready audit exports and no external security product required.


Description:
SCIP unifies software composition analysis (SCA), supply chain risk monitoring, and AI threat detection in one Splunk app. Ingest SBOMs, correlate components against live vulnerability intelligence (OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, EPSS), detect adversarial AI/ML threats with MITRE ATLAS, and assess compliance posture across nine global frameworks — with detection logic written as transparent SPL you can open and read, and no external security product required. CAPABILITIES - SBOM ingestion — file-drop or HEC, supporting CycloneDX (JSON/XML) and SPDX (JSON) - Vulnerability correlation — daily OSV feed (264,944+ records across 5 ecosystems) with PURL-based correlation; NVD CPE-based correlation; CISA KEV matching; EPSS exploit-probability scoring - Supply Chain Risk Score — 0–100 global and per-application risk scoring weighted by severity, KEV status, and EPSS - Vendor Risk — per-vendor risk aggregation and letter-grading across your SBOM portfolio - SBOM Drift Detection — baseline-vs-current component change tracking - License Compliance — GPL/AGPL/copyleft detection and license-risk classification - MITRE ATLAS Detection — 66 detection rules for adversarial AI/ML threats - Silent-Source Detection — alerts when an enrolled AI/LLM telemetry source goes quiet, so a dead pipe is never mistaken for a clean one (Enterprise and Federal Plus) - Compliance Gap Assessment — nine frameworks: PCI DSS 4.0, NIST CSF 2.0, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA Security Rule, EU Cyber Resilience Act, FedRAMP / RMF / CISA, DORA, FDA 524B Premarket Cybersecurity, SEBI CSCRF - Long-Unpatched Critical Exposure — flags critical/high-severity vulnerabilities unpatched 180+ days (all tiers) - POA&M & FedRAMP Workflow — POA&M dashboard, monthly ConMon package builder, BOD 26-04 risk-tier classification (CISA's four-variable model with computed deadlines), deviation request workflow. Dashboards always available; automated POA&M generation is opt-in from Setup - Coverage-Evidence Manifest — AU-12-aligned attestation of unbroken AI-monitoring coverage (Federal Plus) - Audit-ready exports — FedRAMP POA&M Workbook (R3.0 and R2.1), SSP Appendix M Integrated Inventory, Deviation Request Form (Template 2.1 / Aug 2024) - Component Search — instant cross-SBOM component lookup (available in the free Community tier) - Compound Risk — correlates active MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detections with vulnerable components on the same application, surfacing compounding risk neither signal shows alone (Enterprise and Federal Plus) - AI/ML Bill of Materials — catalogs AI/ML model components from your SBOMs (architecture, training data, lineage) with insecure-serialization-format flagging (Professional and above; risk classification on Enterprise and Federal Plus) TIERS Community (free), Professional, Federal, Enterprise, Federal Plus. Feature availability gated by license tier; contact us for tier comparison. SUPPORT GIC Engineering Consultants — contact@gicengineeringconsultants.com

item.title: Appbase version catalogue - v2.1.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Polls the Splunkbase API to maintain a local KV Store catalogue of app versions and provides dashboards to compare installed apps against Splunkbase releases.


Description:
The Splunkbase Version Catalog app builds and maintains a local catalogue of Splunkbase app versions by polling the public Splunkbase API on a scheduled basis. The app records release metadata for tracked applications, including version numbers, release dates, compatible Splunk platform versions, cloud-compatibility flags, FedRAMP status, and archival state. All catalogue data is stored in a KV Store collection keyed by Splunkbase numeric app ID, enabling efficient updates without duplication. Each polling cycle also writes versioned events to an index for historical tracking. Two dashboards provide views into the catalogue: one for browsing all tracked Splunkbase apps and their metadata, and another that compares locally installed apps against their corresponding Splunkbase releases to identify available updates. A saved search automates the detection of outdated installed apps. The app is implemented entirely with the Python 3 standard library, avoiding bundled third-party dependencies to simplify AppInspect vetting for Splunk Cloud Platform deployments.

Short Description:
Renders interactive parent/child topology diagrams in Dashboard Studio with health-based node coloring, drag-to-arrange positioning, and built-in layout persistence stored in dashboard JSON.


Description:
The Topology Visualization app provides a custom Dashboard Studio visualization that renders parent/child topology diagrams directly from search results. The visualization displays a root or hub node at the center with child nodes radiating outward, automatically colored and scored based on health metrics. Built on Splunk's Dashboard Extension framework, the visualization supports interactive node positioning with built-in layout persistence that stores custom layouts directly in the dashboard JSON as standard visualization options. The app enables dashboard interactivity through click-driven token setting, allowing users to trigger actions and filter content based on node selection. Layout persistence operates without requiring KV Store collections, macros, or custom search commands, functioning through the native Dashboard Studio persistence layer. Users can drag nodes to create custom layouts in view mode, and administrators can publish these layouts to all users by switching to edit mode and saving without reloading the browser tab.

Description:
Data Heartbeat monitors your Splunk environment for source types that have stopped sending data. When a data source goes silent — whether from a misconfigured forwarder, a failed log shipper, or a broken integration — Data Heartbeat detects the gap and alerts you before the silence becomes a blind spot. Every monitored source type has a configurable threshold, measured in minutes. When no data arrives within that window, the app flags the source type and fires your chosen alert action: Slack, Microsoft Teams, a generic webhook, or email via Splunk's built-in SMTP relay. Key features: • Monitor dashboard — a live status table showing every tracked source type, the minutes since its last event, its threshold, and its importance level, with color-coded severity (green, yellow, red, and critical). • Per-row alert actions — each source type can use its own notification target, independent of the global default. • Auto Discovery — a nightly scan that surfaces new source types appearing in your environment and queues them for review. • Importance tagging — mark business-critical sources as High, Medium, or Low importance. When a high-importance source goes silent, the app raises a red-alert banner. • Settings page — configure global defaults (threshold, alert action, and notification target), enable or disable the monitoring pipeline, and test alert actions without waiting for a real outage. • Audit log — a full history of every configuration change, with timestamps and user attribution. • No index footprint — all configuration is stored in KV Store, so no custom indexes are required.
